newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Belka sees pension bills ready in April.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Belka sees pension bills ready in April.

text.p: Poland's cabinet will probably send parliament in April the majority of bills necessary for the reform of the country's ailing state pension system, Finance Minister Marek Belka told the daily Parkiet in its Saturday edition.

"Currently we're at the home stretch....That doesn't mean it was possible to reach unanimity on all points (on pension reform) but I believe that in April the majority of bills will reach parliament," he was quoted as saying.

The labour ministry has promised to complete four bills triggering the pension reform by the end of March but many observers say the bills, even if approved by the government, could get stuck in parliament during this election year.

Poland's current bureaucratic and inefficient communist-era system is seen posing a serious threat to public finances as the number of pensioners is set to rise from the current nine million to 11 million in 2010.

Belka, who became finance minister last month when his predecessor stepped down to avoid the pre-election political fray, has said he would pay special attention to the overhaul of the social security system.
